traceability.notes: The story describes an ESLint rule that validates significant code branches (if/else, try/catch, switch, loops) have @story and @req annotations, with configurability, nested-structure support, and performance considerations.,Core functionality (detection of missing annotations on branches) is fully implemented in src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts and src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts and is extensively exercised by tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts. The rule inspects all configured branch node types and reports missing @story/@req with appropriate auto-fixes.,Comment association (including tricky SwitchCase layouts and both line/block comments) is implemented via gatherBranchCommentText and validated by specific tests (e.g., "valid fallback scanning comment detection" and other valid/invalid cases). This satisfies REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION and REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING.,Significance criteria are captured by DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES covering if, switch cases, try/catch, and loops, aligned with the story’s definition. REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE is implemented by validateBranchTypes, with clear configuration error messages when invalid types are supplied; both helper and rule-level tests validate this behavior.,Nested structures and complex branching are handled naturally by the visitor-based design; tests explicitly cover nested if-statements (valid and invalid) and a large nested-branch synthetic file in performance tests. Performance constraints (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION) are enforced by the perf test that asserts analysis of a large nested-branch file completes under a 5-second budget.,User-experience aspects are addressed: the rule’s message `Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.` clearly states which annotation is missing and why the branch is being flagged; auto-fixers insert placeholder @story/@req comments in intuitive locations, and configuration error messages enumerate allowed branch types. This aligns with the User Experience and Error Handling acceptance criteria.,Documentation exists and is aligned with implementation: docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md describes behavior, configuration, valid/invalid examples, and configuration error messages consistent with the code and tests. The rule is integrated into the plugin’s rule registry and default flat-config presets, ensuring it is available and enabled in typical usage.,All relevant tests for this story (behavior, configuration, helpers, performance) pass in the full test run, providing concrete, executable confirmation that the acceptance criteria and listed requirements for docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are satisfied.
